script: Ladybird, a browser built on a brand-new engine, is now available to test. Its developer, Andreas Kling, announced the alpha release on Monday. It runs on macOS and Linux after more than four years of work. This makes it the first browser in years with an entirely new engine. An engine is the core software that turns web code into the pages you see. Today most browsers rely on just three engines: Gecko, Blink, and WebKit. Gecko powers Firefox, WebKit powers Safari, and Blink powers Chrome and Edge. Ladybird is backed by a nonprofit that wants a fast, private, independent browser. The project started in C++ and later moved its code to Rust with help from AI. Kling calls the alpha build modest but functional. He warns that some websites will not work during this early alpha stage. A Windows version is planned for a later stage of the project.
